entries.clue: To intimidate Balls, one needs Private Eye (7)

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls
a = one
the magazine speaks of itself in the editorial 'we'

annotation.surface: A jibe that the Labour politician Ed Balls could only be cowed by the satirical magazine.
annotation.walkthrough: Balls is Ed Balls in the surface, but the capital hides a cricket over. Private Eye, which prints this puzzle, stands for the editorial WE it writes in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to awe someone so thoroughly that they are cowed is to intimidate them.

entries.clue: Book showing pop singer's bottom half in dancing move (6)

indicatorNotes.bottom half: takes the second half of the word
indicatorNotes.dancing: a move that is dancing is jigging about, so its letters will not keep their places

blocks.note: MOVE rearranged to VOME, split round the insert
the second half of LULU, the Scottish pop singer
the rest of VOME

annotation.surface: Someone writing about a singer's hip movements on the dance floor.
annotation.walkthrough: The pop singer is Lulu, whose name halves neatly into LU and LU.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in the numbered volumes of an encyclopedia, each a separate book.

entries.clue: Suspect ranted about Brown having being dismissed? (9)

indicatorNotes.Suspect: letters that are dubious need rearranging

blocks.note: RANTED rearranged to REDANT; its first two letters
dun is a dull greyish brown
the rest of the rearranged REDANT

annotation.surface: Gordon Brown, the former Labour Prime Minister, blamed in a rant for someone's sacking.
annotation.walkthrough: Brown is the ex-PM in the surface and a plain colour in the wordplay. The question mark flags a definition by example: being made redundant is one way of being dismissed.
annotation.definitionFit: A worker made redundant has been dismissed because the job is no longer needed.

entries.clue: Sort of thinking "Wife is hard and not quite satisfied" (7)

indicatorNotes.not quite: the word falls just short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
used as it stands
as on pencils
FULL, satisfied after a meal, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A husband's hopeful reading of his wife's verdict on their love life.
annotation.walkthrough: Wishful thinking is the phrase, so the definition only makes sense read with the word it pairs with.
annotation.definitionFit: Wishful thinking is one sort of thinking: believing what you would like to be true.

entries.clue: X, an unsuitable child worker (7)

blocks.note: X is the sign for a kiss at the foot of a letter
someone who hits children should not be working with them

annotation.surface: A terse note on a job applicant marked X as unfit for childcare.
annotation.walkthrough: X looks like a cross on a form, rejecting the candidate; it is the kiss at the end of a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Smacker is slang for a noisy kiss, which X stands for.

entries.clue: Get laid – and be discerning! (4,3)

blocks.note: slang for having a sexual encounter
discerning here is perceiving, as with a shape in the dark

annotation.surface: Advice to be both promiscuous and choosy.
annotation.walkthrough: Discerning looks like 'choosy' but means seeing: making out a shape.
annotation.definitionFit: Make out covers both senses: getting intimate and managing to perceive.

entries.clue: Big noise's family money (5)

blocks.note: a clan is an extended family
G = grand, a thousand pounds

annotation.surface: A remark about an important person's family fortune.
annotation.walkthrough: A big noise is slang for an important person, which is what the surface wants; here it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing metallic noise.

entries.clue: (& 12ac.) Choice show-ring? Empty promises no doubt (8)

blocks.note: an election is a choosing
to manifest is to show
a ring is O-shaped

annotation.surface: A cynic's view that a showy party pitch is full of empty promises.
annotation.walkthrough: Show-ring looks like one word, an arena for animals; split it and each half gives a piece.
annotation.definitionFit: An election manifesto is a party's list of promises, cynically assumed empty.

entries.clue: Dressed as a Young Conservative? (4)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a lad is a young man

annotation.surface: Asking whether someone is dressed up as a Young Conservative.
annotation.walkthrough: Young Conservatives were the youth wing of Britain's Conservative Party; the letters are read in the order C then LAD.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the old past participle of 'clothe', still used as in 'leather-clad'.

entries.clue: Hair rollers producing explosive results? (5,5)

blocks.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass of it
rollers are long breaking waves at sea

annotation.surface: Curlers in the hair giving a dramatic hairdo.
annotation.walkthrough: Hair rollers are curlers in the surface; split them and each word is a separate piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Shock waves are the pressure fronts sent out by an explosion.

entries.clue: Bar causes stink over street disturbance (11)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, turning over flips the letters

blocks.note: BO, body odour, turned over
standard abbreviation
a ruction is a noisy row

annotation.surface: A pub whose smell sets off trouble in the street outside.
annotation.walkthrough: Bar is a pub in the surface and a barrier in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A bar is something that blocks the way, an obstruction.

entries.clue: see 8dn. (9)
Bottle internal organs (4)

blocks.note: bottle is British slang for courage
the intestines

annotation.surface: Organs preserved in a jar.
annotation.walkthrough: Bottle looks like a container; in British slang it means nerve, as in 'lost his bottle'.
annotation.definitionFit: Guts means courage and also the bowels.

entries.clue: 'Whiteness' spin by a political leader rebounded (6)

indicatorNotes.leader: the first letter leads the word
indicatorNotes.rebounded: bounced back, so the whole sequence runs backwards

blocks.note: a roll is a spin
used as it stands
first letter of political

annotation.surface: A party's spin about something called 'whiteness' backfiring on its leader.
annotation.walkthrough: Build ROLL, A, P, then turn the lot round.
annotation.definitionFit: Pallor is paleness of the face, a whiteness.

entries.clue: Drug depression's over – super! (6)

indicatorNotes.over: turned over, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: pot is cannabis
a pit is a hollow in the ground

annotation.surface: Delight that a drug-induced low has passed.
annotation.walkthrough: Depression is a mood in the surface and a hole in the ground in the wordplay; POTPIT turned round gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Tiptop means excellent, first-rate.

entries.clue: Right way of going about interrupting Lords member who's putting on an act (9)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: breaks into another word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: PEER, a member of the House of Lords, opened up
standard abbreviation
form is the proper way of doing something
the rest of PEER

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a relative clause; read it as 'one who's putting on an act'
annotation.surface: A peer who is only pretending during a debate in the House of Lords.
annotation.walkthrough: Member looks as if it belongs with who's putting on an act; it is part of the wordplay, and the definition is the clause after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A performer is someone who puts on an act for an audience.

entries.clue: Part of the whole embarrassment of 'relating' (8)

indicatorNotes.embarrassment of: the letters are thrown into confusion

blocks.note: RELATING rearranged

annotation.surface: Awkwardness felt about some family relationship.
annotation.walkthrough: Embarrassment usually means shame; here it is a mess the letters are in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an element needed to make something complete belongs to it as a part of the whole.

entries.clue: Arch is complying with party whip's orders? (6)

blocks.note: the arched middle of the foot
marching to the party's beat, like soldiers on parade

annotation.surface: An arch-loyalist doing exactly what the party whip says.
annotation.walkthrough: A whip is the MP who enforces party discipline in a vote; a loyal member stays in step.
annotation.definitionFit: The instep is the arched part of the foot.

entries.clue: Mate's scrap with inept type getting end away (7)

indicatorNotes.getting end away: the last letter is sent off

blocks.note: a scrap is a part of something
NERD without its last letter

annotation.surface: A fight with a hapless character, with a bawdy hint that the answer's mate is having sex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting your end away' is British slang for having sex; here it just drops the end of NERD.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a mate in life, a business or a game is the person paired with you.

entries.clue: Former leader thrown out – right has ball (6)

blocks.note: cast = thrown
standard abbreviation
a ball is O-shaped

annotation.surface: A deposed leader, with the political right celebrating.
annotation.walkthrough: Thrown out reads as deposed, apt for the man; it only means cast.
annotation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led Cuba for decades.

entries.clue: Chief corruption of Euro MPs (7)

indicatorNotes.corruption of: the letters are spoilt out of their order

blocks.note: EURO MPS rearranged

annotation.surface: Allegations of graft among members of the European Parliament.
annotation.walkthrough: Chief looks like an adjective qualifying corruption; it is a noun, the definition, standing alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge.

entries.clue: Neutralise Dicky with fix (6)

blocks.note: dicky is British slang for unwell or unsound, i.e. off
to set is to fix in place

annotation.surface: Defusing someone called Dicky by rigging things.
annotation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name thanks to its capital; in British slang it means dodgy, as a dicky heart.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cancelling out one effect with an equal and opposite one neutralises it.

entries.clue: Party faction abandoned (4)

blocks.note: the socialist wing of a party
past tense of leave, as in deserted

annotation.surface: A group within a party that has been cast aside.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one idea, a faction dumped by its party; split it after faction into two separate definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: The left is a party's left wing; left also means abandoned.

entries.clue: "Gutted" Conservative keeping mum about corporation (5)

indicatorNotes.Gutted: the insides are removed, leaving the outside
indicatorNotes.about: the letters are turned about into a new order

blocks.note: TORY with its insides gone leaves T...Y
MUM rearranged
the other end of TORY

annotation.surface: A Tory staying silent about a big company, and gutted about it.
annotation.walkthrough: Mum here is the mother, not silence, and about scrambles her. Corporation is dated British slang for a pot belly.
annotation.definitionFit: A corporation is a large paunch, which is a tummy.

entries.clue: Such gear needed by 'wets' for pain or distress (9)

blocks.note: FOR PAIN OR rearranged

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes gear; RAINPROOF is the adjective for it
annotation.surface: Tory moderates, the 'wets', needing protection from pain.
annotation.walkthrough: Wets were Thatcher-era moderate Conservatives; here they are just people getting rained on.
annotation.definitionFit: Rainproof gear keeps off the rain, which is what those getting wet need.

entries.clue: Ex-Trump sidekick kidnaps minor – perversely to achieve celebrity status (10)

indicatorNotes.perversely: the letters go the wrong way, out of order

blocks.note: Mike PENCE, Trump's first Vice-President, opened up
MINOR rearranged
the rest of PENCE

annotation.surface: A former Trump deputy abducting a child in a warped bid for fame.
annotation.walkthrough: Perversely sits by the kidnapping for the surface, but it only works on MINOR, scrambling it before it goes inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Prominence is the state of being famous or noticeable.

entries.clue: Rocket man's particular odour? (4)

blocks.note: Elon, the billionaire whose SpaceX builds rockets
a strong animal scent, taken from a small Asian deer and used in perfume

annotation.definitionNote: the first definition is possessive; read it as 'Rocket man'
annotation.surface: Wondering what a rocket magnate smells like.
annotation.walkthrough: Rocket man sounds like the Elton John song; it is the SpaceX owner.
annotation.definitionFit: Elon Musk runs a rocket company, and musk is a heavy scent.

entries.clue: Prince bonkers for luvvies? (7)

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
bonkers read as 'people who bonk', i.e. lay

annotation.surface: A crazy prince being mad about actors.
annotation.walkthrough: Bonkers wants to mean mad; read it as a noun, people who bonk (British slang for have sex). Luvvies is British slang for gushing actors.
annotation.definitionFit: Luvvies is British slang for theatrical actors, and players is the old word for actors.

entries.clue: Have help being creative with entry in erotic novel (2-5)

indicatorNotes.entry in: an entry is something let in, so the piece before it goes inside what follows
indicatorNotes.novel: new, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: EROTIC rearranged to CORITE, split round the insert
standard abbreviation
the rest of CORITE

annotation.surface: Getting a hand with the steamy parts of a racy novel.
annotation.walkthrough: Novel is a book in the surface but works as 'new' on EROTIC.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose paraphrase: sharing authorship of a piece means having help with the creative work.
